content: The Magnificent Mei and Friends comic series and its accompanying Teacher’s Guide were developed as part of the Helping Adolescents Thrive (HAT) initiative, a collaborative effort by the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF. This initiative was led by the WHO Departments of Mental Health and Substance Use, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health and Ageing, and UNICEF’s Health Section. The development team included experts such as Joanna Lai, Sarah Watts, Tanvi Jain, Batool Fatima, Chiara Servili, and Tarun Dua, among others. The comic illustrations were created by Aizat Zhunusova, with contributions from professionals across various countries, including Nepal, South Africa, Ghana, and others. The materials were reviewed by a diverse group of experts from WHO, UNICEF, and other organizations. The Teacher’s Guide and comic series aim to promote social and emotional learning (SEL) among adolescents aged 10–14 years. By fostering SEL, the materials seek to enhance psychosocial well-being, prevent mental health conditions, and reduce risky behaviors in adolescents. SEL is defined as the process through which individuals acquire and apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to manage emotions, develop healthy identities, show empathy, maintain supportive relationships, and make responsible decisions. The guide is structured into three main parts: 1. Key Concepts: This section provides foundational knowledge about mental health and well-being, with a focus on adolescents. It addresses common myths and facts about mental health, the unique challenges faced by adolescents, and the importance of early intervention to promote positive mental health. 2. Essentials for Teachers: This section offers practical guidance on how teachers can effectively communicate with adolescents, build strong teacher-student relationships, manage their own well-being, and identify when students may need additional mental health support. It emphasizes the importance of active listening, empathy, and creating a safe and open classroom environment. 3. Classroom Lesson Plans and Activities: This section includes short lesson plans and activities designed to complement the comic series. These activities aim to engage students in discussions about mental health, social skills, and emotional regulation. The materials highlight the critical role teachers play in supporting adolescent mental health. Teachers are uniquely positioned to help students develop social and emotional skills, which are essential for navigating school, relationships, and life challenges. Adolescence is a pivotal period for mental health, as half of all mental health conditions begin before the age of 14. Early adolescence, in particular, represents a crucial window for intervention to prevent the onset of mental health conditions and promote resilience. The guide also addresses common misconceptions about mental health, such as the belief that mental illness is a sign of weakness or that it only affects certain groups of people. It emphasizes that mental health conditions can affect anyone, regardless of socioeconomic status or background, and that seeking help requires strength and courage. The materials encourage teachers to reflect on their own perspectives about mental health and to challenge any biases that may influence their interactions with students. By fostering a culture of understanding and support, teachers can help reduce stigma and create an environment where students feel comfortable seeking help when needed. The guide is not intended to replace professional mental health care or treatment. Teachers are advised to refer students to appropriate mental health services if they exhibit signs of severe distress, such as suicidal thoughts, self-harm, or overwhelming fear. The guide also provides tips for building rapport with students, such as showing genuine interest in their opinions, practicing active listening, and maintaining professional boundaries. The HAT initiative emphasizes the importance of universal mental health promotion and prevention strategies for adolescents. By equipping teachers with the tools and knowledge to support adolescent mental health, the initiative aims to help young people thrive and reach their full potential.
